desc:
A trading system keeps a backlog of unmatched orders. Each incoming order is [price, amount, type] where type = 0 is a buy and type = 1 is a sell. Orders arrive in the given sequence and are processed one by one:

  • A buy order matches against the sell orders in the backlog whose price is at most its price, always taking the cheapest sell order first.
  • A sell order matches against the buy orders in the backlog whose price is at least its price, always taking the most expensive buy order first.
  • A match trades min(amounts) units and removes them from both orders; keep matching while units remain and a matching order exists.
  • Whatever is left of the incoming order is added to the backlog.

After all orders have been processed, return the total number of units still in the backlog, modulo 1,000,000,007.

orders = [[10,5,0],[15,2,1],[25,1,1],[30,4,0]]
buy 5 @10 -> backlog
sell 2 @15: needs a buy ≥ 15, none -> backlog
sell 1 @25 -> backlog
buy 4 @30: sells ≤ 30 are @15 (2) and @25 (1): trades 2 then 1, 1 unit left -> backlog
backlog: buy 5 @10, buy 1 @30 -> total 6
hints: The backlog never contains a buy and a sell that could trade with each other, so the two sides can be stored separately.
For a new buy you repeatedly need the cheapest sell; for a new sell you repeatedly need the most expensive buy. That is a min-heap and a max-heap.

Keep a min-heap of sells (price, amount) and a max-heap of buys (store the negated price). Match while possible, pushing back the unfinished part of the order at the top if it is only partly used, then add what remains of the incoming order. At the end sum the amounts in both heaps modulo 1,000,000,007.
editorial: After every step the backlog is stable: its best buy price is strictly below its best sell price. A new buy can only trade with the cheapest sells, a new sell only with the highest buys, so each side needs a priority queue ordered by the price that matters first.

Each loop iteration either removes an order completely from a heap or finishes the incoming order, so the number of heap operations is bounded by a constant times the number of orders: every order is pushed at most once (plus at most one re-push after a partial match). The time is O(n log n).
The total amount can reach 5 × 10<sup>12</sup>, hence the modulo; in a fixed-width language accumulate the sum in a 64-bit type or reduce while adding.
